final_answer:
The Rosetta Stone holds immense significance as a pivotal artifact in the study of ancient Egypt. It features a decree issued in 196 BCE, inscribed in three scripts: Ancient Greek, Demotic (a form of Egyptian script used for everyday purposes), and Egyptian hieroglyphs. This trilingual text was crucial because it allowed scholars to compare the scripts and decipher hieroglyphs, which had been undecipherable for centuries.

The key to unlocking hieroglyphs lay in the Greek text, which was already well understood. By aligning the Greek words with their corresponding hieroglyphic symbols, scholars, notably Jean-François Champollion in the 1820s, could begin to identify the phonetic and symbolic meanings of hieroglyphs. This breakthrough revealed that hieroglyphs were not purely symbolic but also represented sounds, blending logographic and phonetic elements.

The Rosetta Stone thus opened the door to understanding ancient Egyptian literature, history, and culture, transforming the study of the civilization and providing insights into its religious beliefs, governance, and daily life.
